additions, so that the <term>quinta essentia</term> <gloss>fifth essence</gloss> remains in their scent, color, and taste, and that it may increase in these and not diminish, as in musk, ambergris, and civet. If the fifth essence of these is extracted, you will notice the body <note>the remaining physical substance</note> stinks and is of no importance, neither in taste, nor in scent, nor in nature. The same must be judged regarding the extraction of the fifth essence of all other things. Although musk, ambergris, and civet are not referred to this present chapter, because we describe those things specifically and here we deal only with those things that grow <note>plants or herbs</note>, such as lilies, lavender, and leaves: the process of their extraction is as follows.

Take the growing things well crushed, which, having been placed in a pot in horse manure, digest for four weeks, and distill by a <term>balneum</term> <gloss>water bath</gloss>; afterwards, putrefy them again in horse manure for eight days, and distill again by the bath: the fifth essence will transcend through the alembic, and the body will remain at the bottom. But if more fifth essence were to be held in the bottom, proceed by putrefying and distilling. Afterward, take the distilled water and add that growing thing to it again, and digest for six days by a <term>pellicanum</term> <gloss>a vessel for circulation</gloss>, and it will turn into a dense color, which you must strain; distill the strained liquid by the bath, and the body will come forth, but the fifth essence will reside at the bottom, which you must separate by the press of a <term>retorta</term> <gloss>retort</gloss> from the dregs, and allow the fifth essence [to settle for] four

<summary>This page describes the extraction of the fifth essence from plant matter, emphasizing that the vital qualities of scent, color, and taste are lost if the process is not performed correctly, and provides a specific laboratory procedure using horse manure and distillation.</summary>
<keywords>Fifth essence, quintessence, alchemy, distillation, putrefaction, plant extraction, Paracelsus</keywords>
